## 2026-10-28 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign: smoke-test finding 5, banded pixel-layer adjustments

Owner request: "okay lets fix it i really wan to move on to the next thing so lets close this and anything else that comes up just fix it". Committed and pushed on that go-ahead.

**Investigation:**
- A temporary probe (counting `#[global_allocator]`, deleted, never committed) on a 6000×4000 filled document showed `image.adjustments.levels` peaking at +1560.9 MB and keeping +96 MB (the undo copy of the layer).
- Cause: photocraft `pixels::adjust_surface` (private, called from `destructive_adjust`) allocates `raw`, `buf`, `orig` and `out` over the layer's whole `content_bounds()`. photocraft is a git dependency and isn't edited.

**Fix** (`xdesign_photo_adjust.rs`):
- `execute` sends pixel layers (`Ok(None)` from the coverage check) to the new `pixel_layer`.
- `pixel_layer` returns `None`, keeping the engine route, when `engine.disabled_reason(command)` is set, the channel target is `ChannelTarget::Color(_)`, or the active layer isn't `LayerContent::Raster`.
- It replicates the engine: `adjust_params::from_params(kind, params, None, mode)`; the active layer (the engine ignores `params.layer`); the whole `content_bounds()`, unpruned; `mask_filters::edit_history` with `adjustment.label()`, so coalescing matches `Session::edit`; the journal gets `(command, params)` as given; Fade gets `FadeSource { doc, revision, layer, mask: false, label: undo label or command }`.
- `apply` now takes the document mode for `Transfer::for_document`, decodes each band with photocraft's `read_rgba_into`, reads selection coverage with `read_region`, and no longer prunes (the coverage path prunes itself). Bands are 4096×256, or 40×32 in tests so fixtures cross band edges.
- Dithering in Gradient Map and Color Lookup uses absolute `Buffer` coordinates, so banding doesn't change it. All 16 adjustments are pointwise.

**Rulings:**
- The journal entry stays the engine's (params as given), not `commit_host_edit`'s, which would add `target` and `layer`. Cost if wrong: replay sees a different shape from other host edits.
- `slice_cmds::refresh` and `sync_preset_store` aren't called: an adjustment changes neither alpha-derived slices nor presets.
- Pixel locks aren't checked, which matches the engine.
- No `catch_unwind`, like the other Orion host edits.
- Colour-channel targets keep the engine route and its peak. They're rare, and replicating the channel write path would widen the change.

**Measurements** (6000×4000 RGB8, debug test build, production bands): every adjustment's extra peak went from +1560.9 MB to +136.0 MB, +96 MB kept either way. Levels 1.62 → 2.53 s, Curves 1.81 → 1.72 s, Hue/Saturation 1.45 → 2.09 s, Brightness/Contrast 2.48 → 2.36 s. A first version decoding pixel by pixel in Orion code took 4.5–4.9 s, because Orion is built at opt-level 0 in dev while dependencies are opt-level 3. Release timing wasn't measured.

**Tests** (`xdesign_photo_adjust_pixel_tests.rs`, 4 tests):
- `pixel_layer_adjustments_match_the_engine_in_every_mode_and_depth`: 16 adjustments × 4 modes × 3 depths × selection on/off, on a layer reaching past the canvas with HDR, transparent and partly transparent pixels. Compares result, pixels, history length and label, revision and coalesce, journal, and Fade (document and layer ids per session, since they're process-wide counters); undo restores the layer. Asserts 384 cases ran.
- Invalid params and an empty layer; Fade (40%, Multiply) after a banded adjustment; colour-channel targets and adjustment layers stay on the engine route.
- `cargo test --lib`: 1446 passed, 0 failed, 20 ignored. `rustfmt --check` fails on this file both before and after; no format step is part of the gate, so it was left.

**Docs:** smoke-test finding 5, its status line and the alpha-limits memory line updated.

## 2026-10-28 — Claude / XDesign: Home previews, image-editor resume, names from Save As; builds 26–27

Owner request: real thumbnails on the XDesign Home page ("i picture seeing that project r2c at the top and a preview of the conten like the image that i was working on, when i click it it should basically pic right back up from the last save"). Brainstormed into the spec, planned in 6 tasks, run inline (owner: "just go native"), each step test-first. Committed and pushed on the owner's go-ahead. The ledger in `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-28-xdesign-home-previews/` was deleted after the commit; git history is the record.

**Task 1, top of the list and names from Save As** (`projectsStore.ts`, `photo/runtime.ts`):
- Registry entries carry `nameFromFile`; `DEFAULT_PROJECT_NAME` marks an untouched name.
- `noteImageSaved(projectId, path, saveAs)` runs after a successful image file write. It bumps `updatedAt`. On a Save As, a default or file-derived name takes the file's stem, numbered if another project has it, never counting the project itself. A typed name is left alone.
- `exportImage` calls it.

**Task 2, resume** (`photo/resume.ts`, `photo/types.ts`, `store.ts`, `pluginContributions.ts`, `PhotoStudio.tsx`, `XDesignApp.tsx`, `xdesign_archive.rs`):
- `photoResume` (legacy shape id, or Pencil node id plus photo document id) is saved beside `photoDocuments`, so undo can't change it, and checked on load by `validatePhotoResume`.
- `startOpenImageTracking` records it while the image editor is open; `closeImageEditor` clears it on a user close.
- `resumeImageEditor()` returns `Promise<boolean>`; XDesignApp retries when the Pencil editor arrives. It does nothing for FX and 3D projects, and checks `pencilEditorProject()` so a leftover editor can't clear the new project's image.
- `local_only()` drops `photoResume` from exports, clones and imports.

**Task 3, storage** (`src-tauri/src/xdesign_preview.rs`, `lib.rs`):
- `xdesign_preview_write(projectId, png)`, `xdesign_preview_list()`, `xdesign_preview_delete(projectId)`.
- Ids must round-trip as a ULID. Writes are capped at 4 MiB, must start with the PNG signature, and use `atomic_write_bytes`. Listing skips anything that isn't `<ULID>.png`. `revision` is the file's mtime in µs.
- 3 Rust tests.

**Task 4, capture** (`projectPreview.ts`, `previewCapture.ts`, `previewImage.ts`, `pencil/runtime.ts` `capturePencilPreview`, `projectsStore.ts`, `XDesignApp.tsx`):
- `captureProjectPicture` picks, in order: nothing unless active; "clear" while the Claude page is open; FX via `renderFxSnapshot` at t=0; 3D via `captureReviewShot`; the resumable image's preview; the Pencil board (rendered from a decoded copy of autosave's cached graph); the legacy board.
- `startPreviewTracking` (mounted by XDesignApp) watches the active id and its `updatedAt`, input events, and the photo and Pencil busy flags. Captures don't register XDesign activity, so they never block a project change.
- A switch marks a running capture abandoned. Its result is dropped, and the project is captured again when it's next active.
- `leaveActive()` (open, Home, close of the active tab) saves, then `settlePreview` with a 400 ms budget. `deleteProject` removes the preview after the commit.
- 11 + 7 tests, plus 2 in `projectsStore.test.ts`.

**Task 5, Home** (`XDesignHome.tsx`, `tokens.css`):
- Loads the preview list on mount. Cards with an entry render `img.xd-home-card-image` at `convertFileSrc(path)?v=<revision>`. `onError` falls back to `ProjectThumb` for that revision.
- Full docs load only after the list, and only for design projects with no entry.
- `.xd-home-card-image` sets no colour or spacing, so no tokens were needed.
- 3 tests. `ProjectImportRecovery.runtime.test.tsx` now answers `xdesign_preview_list` and counts only import-control calls.

**Rulings** (all in the ledger, each with its cost if wrong):
- No worktree, no commits; reviewed from the working-tree diff.
- `pencilEditorProject()`; resume returns a boolean; resume skips FX/3D; the PhotoStudio close test goes through File › Close.
- `projectPreview` is lazy from `projectsStore` and imports `previewCapture` statically; Pencil captures from a copy; any switch abandons a capture; it polls every 1.5 s while blocked; `load()` outside Tauri does nothing.
- The recovery test counts only its own native calls.

**Gates:**
- Typecheck clean.
- 9 focused files pass, 191/191. A first run beside the `cargo` compile had 3 `PhotoStudio.tools` timeouts at 5 s; that file alone passed 81/81, and the final run passed clean.
- `cargo test --lib` 1442 passed, 20 ignored.
- Build 26 (`/Users/lucaorion/Orion_Terminal/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Orion Terminal.app`) starts on `HOME=/tmp/xd-release-home` and opens its window with an empty log; it was then quit. `/Applications` was not replaced.
- No UI automation: `AXIsProcessTrusted` is false in this session.

**Final review** (a fresh opus reviewer, whole working-tree diff): "With fixes", 0 Critical, 2 Important, 5 Minor, and 10 items it declined to judge. I re-graded them by what a person gets:
- **Fixed, Important 1:** `renderFxSnapshot` freed its GL objects but never its WebGL context, so each FX capture left one alive, and WebKit drops the oldest, which can be the open FX editor's. It now calls `WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()` after `dispose()`. This also covers FxEditor's snapshot exports. Test: `fx/fxExport.snapshot.test.ts`.
- **Fixed, Important 2, legacy half:** a legacy board capture rendered each photo at full resolution (`xdesign_photo_render`), then read and base64-encoded it on the main thread. `rasterizePNG`/`renderPngBytes` take `fullResolutionPhotos` (default true, so the Claude vision picture is unchanged), and previews pass false, keeping the board's own preview hrefs. Tests: 2 in `exportXD.resource.test.ts`, and `previewCapture.test.ts` expects the flag.
- **Ruled, Important 2, Pencil half:** a Pencil capture still decodes a copy of the graph, image bytes included, on the main thread. Avoiding the copy means rendering the live graph, which reads as an edit (Task 4 ruling). Unmeasured; there's a new owner-checklist line for it.
- **Declined items, all ruled to stand, with costs in the ledger:**
  - a tab switch during a resume is refused with a message;
  - opening an image moves its project to the top;
  - each activation takes one capture;
  - the export text-measurer swap can only overlap on a session's first capture;
  - checkpoint restore carries resume and save paths;
  - a mid-capture delete is unreachable;
  - a typed "Untitled N" can be renamed by Save As;
  - legacy previews use the dark editor backdrop;
  - builds 24–25 weren't in this diff.
  - The full-resolution `render.png` on a first legacy capture is gone with the fix above.
- **Deferred minors:**
  - a failing capture retries every 15 s;
  - there's no `pencilEditorProject()` guard on the Pencil capture;
  - an unreadable preview shows an empty card, not the shape drawing;
  - orphaned preview files aren't swept;
  - the number-array IPC, and 1 s mtime filesystems repeating a revision.
- **After the fixes:** 14 focused files pass 223/223; typecheck is clean; Rust is unchanged.
- **Build 27:** release bundle at the same path, exit 0. It starts on `HOME=/tmp/xd-release-home`, opens its window in about 6 s with an empty log, and was quit by pid. `/Applications` wasn't touched, and the owner's dev instance was left running.
- **Plan correction:** the self-review's WebGL row now says the context is released too.

**Owner result and commit:** the owner ran the whole checklist and reported "everything was fine". On "looks good lets commit everything", builds 24–27 (the smoke-test fixes, Save As persistence, this spec, plan and feature) went into one commit. The shared hunks couldn't be split without interactive staging. Pushed on "sure lets close this".

**Smoke-test doc:** the status line now covers builds 24–27. There's a new "Home page" checklist block, with a stutter and FX-preview check for the unmeasured capture cost.

## 2026-10-27 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign: smoke-test fixes, builds 24–25

Owner request: "lets fix those problems you found first then ill test". Each fix was made test-first. Uncommitted.

**F1, Levels flicker:**
- **Cause**: OK cleared the live preview overlay at once, while the applied full-resolution image took ~4 s to reach the canvas.
- **Fix**: `PhotoActionDialog` takes an `untilShown` prop, which defaults to settling on the command. PhotoStudio passes its own, which waits for the canvas `imageShown` with a 2 s fallback.
- **Display**: the dialog keeps `held = preview.url` and keeps the portal `<img>` mounted with that src until then.
- **Scope**: Smart Blur, the only gallery-guarded path, uses geometry and never had the overlay.
- **Test**: "keeps the previewed result on the canvas after OK until the applied image is shown".

**F2, shortcut focus:**
- **Cause**: WebKit doesn't focus a clicked button, so a header click left focus on the body. The shell's global hotkeys then took ⌘L.
- **Fix**: a document `mousedown` listener in PhotoStudio. On the next frame, if focus is on the body and the click was inside the same `.ot-window` but outside `.xd-photo`, it focuses `.xd-photo`.
- **Exceptions**: it skips this when a design dialog is open, the window is unfocused or the page lacks focus.

**F3, Save As:**
- `ImageExportDialog` takes `kind: "export" | "copy" | "save"`, which replaces the `copy` boolean. It sets the title (Export As / Save a Copy / Save As), the format list and the OK label.
- PhotoStudio keeps a module-level `savedPaths` map from document id to the last Save As PSD.
- **⌘S**: saves to that PSD, else to an opened PSD, else opens Save As.
- **File menu**: Save As… ⇧⌘S goes after Save.
- **Follow-up, build 25** (owner: "fix that saving issue"):
  - **Bug**: the in-memory map reset on restart, after which ⌘S fell back to `originalPath` and could save over the opened PSD rather than the Save As copy.
  - **Where it lives**: `useXDesign.photoSavePaths` is persisted in the project doc and validated by `validatePhotoSavePaths` (ULID keys, PSD/PSB values, at most 1024 entries). It is a separate map because photo documents are versioned snapshots that undo restores. A field on them could bring back an older Save As path and overwrite the wrong file.
  - **Recording**: `exportImage(path, quality, saveAs)` writes the map inside the export operation, after the native export succeeds. That operation blocks project switches. It also prunes ids that are no longer in `photoDocuments`.
  - **Autosave**: `pluginContributions` schedules a save when the map changes.
  - **Archives**: `local_only()` in `xdesign_archive.rs` drops the map in `build_archive_with_photo_sources` (export, clone) and `unpack_archive_managed` (any import, including crafted files), so an imported project can't point ⌘S at an arbitrary path.
  - **Tests**: `savePaths.test.ts` (persistence through undo and rehydration, exports and non-PSD saves left out, validation). The Rust round-trip test now covers export, crafted import and clone. In `PhotoStudio.tools.test.tsx`, `exportImage` expectations now include the flag.
  - **Gates**: `cargo test --lib` passes (1439). Build 25 is at `/tmp/xd-build25.log`.

**F4, project status:**
- `ProjectChangeStatus` shows `role="status"` "Loading project…" 500 ms after `useXDProjects.transitioning` turns true. Its timer resets on each change.
- `XDesignApp` now renders `<><XDesignWorkspace/><ProjectChangeStatus/></>`, so the status sits outside the inert `.xd-root`.
- **CSS** (`tokens.css`): `.xd-project-status` uses only existing shell tokens: `--glass-bg-strong`, `--glass-border`, `--r-pill`, `--shadow-window`, `--t-secondary` and `--f-mono`.

**F7 and F8:**
- **Thumbnail**: type layers render a `Type` icon thumb (`.xd-photo-layer-type-thumb`).
- **Properties**: the Typography inspector section moved to just after `TransformSection`.
- **Layout test fixture**: needs `bounds` for Transform to render.

**Not fixed:**
- F5, memory: not investigated.
- F6, one image per editor: single-`documentId` architecture.

**Gates:**
- Typecheck is clean.
- Focused vitest, 529 tests in 9 suites: PhotoActionDialog, PhotoStudio.tools, PhotoStudio.layout, ImageDialogs, fileMenu.studio, PhotoTextGeometryDialog, AdjustmentProperties, LayerStyleDialog and ProjectChangeStatus.
- **Build 24** (`npm run tauri build -- --bundles app`, log `/tmp/xd-build24.log`) runs on the scratch HOME.
- **Live check not possible**: `screencapture` reports "could not create image from display", and osascript and axt get no assistive access.

**Docs:**
- The smoke-test doc gives each finding's status. The alpha limits drop the fixed items and add the Save As restart caveat.
- In the parity spec §2.3, the ⇧⌘S "wrong today" clause was removed.

**2. Guides submenu** (`PhotoStudio.tsx`, `viewGuides.ts`, `viewAids.studio.test.tsx`):
- `viewGuides.ts`'s private `inside` is now the exported `guideInside`: the engine's rule that a guide lies strictly between an artboard's edges on its own axis.
- `PhotoStudio.tsx` subscribes to the image's guides (`storedGuides`, defaulting to `[]` outside the selector, so the selector never returns a fresh array). It disables:

  - The artboard test checks the states after each clear: [on, off, on] after clearing the artboard's guides, and [on, on, off] after clearing the canvas guides.

**3. HDR Pro Base Image** (`MergeDialogs.tsx`, `MergeDialogs.test.tsx`):
- **Source order** (checked):
  - `derive` starts from an empty `Session::new()`.
  - `merge_sources` adds the current image, then each file.
  - The engine's `load_sources` reads `s.documents()` in that order, and `ghostBase` indexes it. An index past the end is refused.
  - With no `ghostBase`, `hdr::merge` picks the image with the most well-exposed pixels.
- **Options step**: a Base Image select, enabled only with Remove ghosts. It lists Automatic, then the source names. `ghostBase` is sent only when Remove ghosts is on and an image is chosen.
- **Test**: the first HDR test now adds the open image, checks the list is [Automatic, room.jpg, -2.tif, 0.tif, +2.tif], picks 0.tif and expects `ghostBase: 2` with `useOpenDocuments: true`.

**Not done, and why:**
- **HDR curve**: the engine's tone mapping takes a curve, but `merge_to_hdr` passes `Vec::new()`.
- **HDR preview**: the engine has no merge preview mode.
- **Folder source**: listing the folder's files, as Photoshop does, needs a native listing command, and `merge_sources` still refuses folders.
- **HDR presets**: the values are unknown, so none were invented.

**Gates:**
- Typecheck is clean.
- viewAids.studio, MergeDialogs, PhotoStudio.layout, fileMenu.studio and PhotoStudio.tools pass 293/293.
- Release build 23 succeeded.

## 2026-10-27 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign: macOS-style menu scrolling, menus clear of the dock; builds 18–19

Owner request: "okay lets do that then see what else we should do". "That" was the open observation: the Window and Edit menus scroll in a 900 pt window. Uncommitted, pending authorisation.

**Cause**:
- XDesign's menus are fixed popups clamped to the in-canvas window, because `.ot-window` clips them. The Window menu needs about 670 px and the Edit menu about 1100 px.
- So the menus showed WebKit's scrollbar, with the last row half-cut under the shell dock.
- Keyboard focus used `preventScroll`, so End or ArrowDown could focus a row out of view.
- Real Photoshop's Edit and Window menus also scroll on a 900 pt screen. The fix is to scroll the way macOS does, not to portal the menus out of the window.

**`EditorMenus.tsx`**:
- `positionPopup` bounds the menu at the top of `.ot-dock-wrap` minus `DOCK_REACH`, when that edge falls inside the host. It ignores zero-sized rects, as in jsdom.
- `Popup` keeps `more {up, down}`, which `measure()` updates after positioning and on every scroll.
- Rows reached from the keyboard go through `focusRow(index, true)`, which scrolls the row into view with one `ROW` (22 px) of margin for the strips. Hovered rows only take focus.
- `scrollWhileOver(direction)` steps `scrollTop` by `ROW` every 60 ms until the end. It also closes any open submenu and moves focus to the menu, so the hovered row's highlight goes away.
- The strips are `aria-hidden` divs with pointer enter/leave handlers. The interval is cleared on unmount.

**`editorMenus.css`**:
- The scrollbar is hidden.
- `.xd-menu-scroll` is `position: sticky` with `top: -4px` / `bottom: -4px` and `margin: 0 -4px`. WebKit measures sticky offsets from the content box, so this pins the strips to the padding edge across the full width.
- A −22 px margin on the inner side gives each strip zero net height, so rows never shift when one appears.
- Checked in Playwright WebKit (webkit-2368) before building.

**Dock reach**:
- Build 18 showed a menu ending 14 px above the dock. That is inside the 24 px proximity in which `Dock.tsx` magnifies its tiles.
- Resting on ▼ grew the Orion tile about 28 px above the dock, over the strip, and the tile took the pointer, so nothing scrolled.
- `DOCK_REACH = 24` is now exported from `useShell.ts`, next to `DOCK_CLEARANCE`. `Dock.tsx` uses it in place of its four literals, and the menus stop above it.

**Tests (`EditorMenus.test.tsx`)**:
- A new describe stubs `clientHeight`, `scrollHeight`, `offsetTop` and `offsetHeight` on the prototypes. It checks:
  - which strips show at the top, middle and end;
  - that the strips carry no role or tabindex;
  - hover scrolling with fake timers, through to the end;
  - the scroll positions End, Home, ArrowDown and typeahead reach.
- `positionPopup` gains a dock test: dock top 520 gives maxHeight 450.

**Live**:
- Build 18:
  - The Window and Edit menus showed ▼ and no scrollbar.
  - End and Home revealed Preferences and Undo.
  - Hovering ▼ triggered the dock defect.
- Build 19:
  - The menu ends 24 px above the dock, with no half-cut row.
  - Hovering ▼ scrolled to the end within 0.5 s, and hovering ▲ scrolled back. The wheel works.
  - The dock still magnifies when hovered directly. The pasteboard menu and Esc are unchanged.
- The test tool `/tmp/pstest/axt` gained `move` (hover) and `home`/`end` key codes.

**Photoshop menu comparison** (from the saved `ps_menus.txt` dump, for the next choice):
- Window:
  - Photoshop has Arrange ▸ and Workspace ▸ at the top, and Application Frame, Options, Tools, Contextual Task Bar and the open documents at the bottom.
  - XDesign lacks Arrange ▸, Application Frame, the document list and Glyphs, and its Workspace ▸ is at the bottom.
  - Brush Settings and Clone Source exist in XDesign, but as a toggle and a Properties section, not as Window items.
- Edit: XDesign lacks Keyboard Shortcuts…, Menus… and Toolbar….
- Out of scope (video, 3D or cloud): Timeline, Libraries, Materials, Comments, Version History and Content Credentials.

## 2026-10-27 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign: app-wide WebKit menu guard, pasteboard colour menu; build 17

Owner request: "1. yes 2. sure if its recommended and 3 lets build it". That meant (1) commit and push the previous batch (done, 96c3c2f), (2) block WebKit's menu app-wide, and (3) build Photoshop's pasteboard right-click colour menu. Items 2 and 3 were committed and pushed with the owner's authorisation.

**WebKit menu guard (`src/lib/pageMenuGuard.ts`)**:
- A document-level `contextmenu` listener calls `preventDefault` unless the target is a typing field or the click lands on selected text.
  - Typing fields are inputs of type text, search, url, tel, email, password or number; textareas; and contenteditable areas, including `contenteditable=false` islands inside them.
  - For selected text, the guard checks the selection range's client rects.
- React handlers run before the document listener, so app menus still open.
- Installed after `installPanelDragGuard()` in `main.tsx`.
- PhotoStudio's root handler now uses the shared `editsText`. Before, `closest("input")` let checkboxes and range sliders show the page menu.
- Tests: `pageMenuGuard.test.ts` has 4 tests. jsdom has no `getClientRects` on Range, so it is stubbed.

**Pasteboard menu**:
- `preferences.ts`:
  - Adds `pasteboard: [Pasteboard x3]`, indexed by screen mode (Standard, Full Screen with Menus, Full Screen).
  - Adds `PASTEBOARD_COLORS`: Black #000000, Dark Gray #282828, Medium Gray #535353 and Light Gray #b8b8b8, approximating Photoshop's greys.
  - Adds `pasteboardFill`, which returns null for Default.
  - Sanitising is per entry. A Custom with no valid hex falls back to Default; a valid custom hex is kept even while another colour is chosen.
- `PhotoStudio.tsx`:
  - The stage's `onContextMenu` ignores the image and otherwise opens a `"pasteboard"` menu.
  - Choices are radio items. The current choice is disabled, and Custom is disabled until a colour has been picked.
  - Select Custom Color… opens the picker as `"pasteboard"`, seeded with the custom colour, else the current fill, else #535353.
  - `choosePasteboard` saves only the current mode's entry and reports a failed save as an error.
  - `.xd-ps-canvas` sets `--xd-ps-pasteboard` when a colour is chosen.
- `photoshop.css`: the stage and hidden crop-shade use `var(--xd-ps-pasteboard, var(--xd-bg))`, and `var(--xd-ps-pasteboard, #000)` in Full Screen.
- Tests:
  - preferences gains 1 test: sanitising and fills.

## 2026-10-27 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign follow-up batch: ruler-unit Properties, snapshot thumbnails, layer right-click, tool hints; builds 15–16

Branch: `validation/alpha-2026-09-14`. Committed and pushed with owner authorisation.

- **Properties in ruler units** (`LayerProperties.tsx`, `TransformSection`): it reads `rulerUnit` and `pointSize` from `usePreferences` and converts with `unitsPerPixel(unit, resolution, pointSize, length)`, the function the rulers use. Percent is of the canvas width for W/X and of the height for H/Y, as on the rulers. Labels are px, in, cm, mm, pt, pica and %. Commits convert back to px, and X/Y moves round to whole pixels. `PhotoStudio` passes `resolution` (`state.resolution ?? 72`).
- **Snapshot thumbnails** (`xdesign_photo_history_snapshots.rs`):
  - Each snapshot renders a 56 px thumbnail, the Layers panel's size, when it is created, using `photocraft_compose::thumbnail` and `tiles::png`. `thumbnail` never enlarges, so small images stay small.
  - The Open row's thumbnail comes from `snapshots::opening`. It uses the document at history index 0, or the current one while there is no past. It returns nothing once the first entry is no longer "Open".
  - It is cached per photo, keyed by the History Brush identity of that state, so state refreshes don't re-render it. The photo state returns it as `historyOpenThumbnail`.
  - `PhotoHistory.tsx` shows the PNGs and falls back to the placeholder icon. When the Open row is current and has no thumbnail, it uses the live preview.
- **Layer-name right-click** (`photo.css`): WebKit selects the word under a right-click before the custom menu opens. `.xd-photo-layer` is now `user-select:none`, with the rename input re-enabled.
- **Tool hints** (`PhotoStudio.tsx`, `toolHint`):
  - Added hints for Spot Healing, Pattern Stamp, History Brush, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Dodge, Burn and Sponge.
  - The Eraser has two: erase to the History source, or to transparency and the background colour.
  - A correction to the previous entry: Brush and Pencil already had hints.
  - A layout test walks every tool in `IMAGE_TOOL_GROUPS` and fails if any shows the generic text.
- **Page reload during the build 15 live check**:
  - Cause: ⌘R had hidden the rulers, so a scripted right-click meant for the ruler landed on the pasteboard (`.xd-photo-stage`). It has no `contextmenu` handler, so WebKit showed its own menu, and the next scripted click hit **Reload**.
  - The system log shows `perform action for menu item`, then `FrameLoader::reload`, at 15:49:28.
  - ⌘R itself was ruled out: Tauri 2.11's default macOS menu has no ⌘R item.
  - The document survived in the native session; only the view was lost.
  - **Fix**: the `.xd-photo` root prevents the default context menu unless the target is inside an `input`, `textarea` or `[contenteditable]`, which keep Cut/Copy/Paste. React bubbles the event through portals, so portaled menus and dialogs are covered too.
  - Not done: Photoshop's own pasteboard right-click, the pasteboard colour menu, is not implemented.
  - Outside the photo workspace, the shell and the other apps still show WebKit's menu, with Reload, on areas that don't handle right-clicks.

## 2026-10-27 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign gap closure: build 11 live re-check, fixes for builds 12–14

Branch: `validation/alpha-2026-09-14`. Committed and pushed with owner authorisation.

- **Permissions root cause**: the agent's shell runs under EMP's LaunchAgent `empd`. macOS TCC assigns Accessibility and Screen Recording to that responsible process, and `empd` is ad-hoc signed, so System Settings can't list or grant it. **Workaround**: `/tmp/pstest/runner.command` is a loop opened in Terminal, which holds both permissions. `t.sh '<cmds>'` queues a job and prints its output. `touch /tmp/pstest/q/stop` ends the loop. `W.sh` takes coordinates relative to the window, `capW.sh` captures the window, and `goR.sh` keeps the idle ≥4 s and frontmost-release-app guards. `axt` gained `f9` (keycode 101); its Escape key is named `esc`.
- **Menubar focus swallowed function keys** (`PhotoStudio.tsx`, key handler): menu choices and dialogs return focus to the menubar title. The pass-through filter there let only printable keys and Escape reach the document, so F5–F8, ⌥F9, ⇧F5 and Delete/Backspace did nothing until the canvas was clicked. Function keys, Delete and Backspace now pass through too. Space, Enter, Tab and the arrow keys stay with the button. Test: the tools suite's "hands Escape and tool keys…" case now presses ⌥F9 on the Window trigger and expects the Actions panel. It fails with the old filter.
- **Copy CSS/SVG rejected by WKWebView** (release only): the promise-valued `ClipboardItem`, started inside the click, still failed with `NotAllowedError`. Nothing in the host touches the pasteboard during the command, and there are no devtools in release, so the exact WebKit rule is unconfirmed. **Fix**: under Tauri the engine's text goes to a new host command, `xdesign_photo_copy_text`, which pipes it to `/usr/bin/pbcopy` with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` (a launchd environment may have no UTF-8 locale). Other platforms get an explicit error. No new dependency. Outside Tauri (browser dev), the WebKit path is unchanged. Test: the layout suite's Copy CSS/SVG case covers the host call and the failure message. There is no native unit test, because one would overwrite the owner's clipboard.
- **Rotate View tile seams**: build 12 first tried overlapping colour tiles by 1 px while turned. Live on build 12 the hairlines remained, about half as bright. **Root cause**: under `rotate()` every tile is anti-aliased on its own, and each tile's `.xd-photo-tile-pixels.has-color` checker sits directly under its own canvas with the same edge. At a partly covered edge pixel the checker shows through, at up to about 25 % of its brightness. That is a conflation artifact, not a gap: the preview canvas under the tiles is already the right colour there. A headless WebKit repro (`/tmp/pstest/seam/`; Playwright WebKit 2368, 2× scale, 36°) measured 3258 seam pixels (peak 39/255) for the original, 1546 (peak 22) for the 1 px overlap, and 0 with the fix. **Fix** (`photo.css`, CSS only): while `.xd-photo-image[data-view-angle]` is set, the tile checker gets `padding:1px; background-clip:content-box`. Its edge then falls under the tile's own canvas, and the preview fills the tile edge. Canvas placement doesn't move, because absolutely positioned children size against the padding box. Over transparent areas, the repro's fixed render was closer to a single-canvas reference at 8359 pixels and worse at 2 (error ≤10). The overlap code and its test were reverted, because the overlap also stretched each tile's pixels by 1/512. There is no jsdom test, because jsdom does no compositing.
  - **Build 13 live**: 0 opaque seam pixels in the measured crop, against 522 on build 12. But transparent areas now showed a broken-checker strip along the tile boundaries. The 1 px gap exposed `.xd-photo-image`'s own checker, which WebKit rasterises out of phase with the tile checkers because the layers sit at fractional offsets. In the repro, counted as pixels differing from the base checker over transparent areas, inset alone gave 8899.
  - **Final fix (build 14)**: each colour tile also renders `.xd-photo-tile-under`. It is a copy of the tile's checker with the same box and `background-position`, and is `display:none` unless the view is turned. While turned it is `z-index:-1`, which puts it in the rotated `.xd-photo-image`'s stacking context: above the image checker and below the preview canvas. The 1 px gap therefore shows the preview where there are pixels, and an in-phase checker where there aren't. The inset rule stays. Repro: 0 opaque seams. The only pixels left differing from base (556) were base's own opaque seam at x≈512, y 198–561. A per-tile copy and one shared container rendered pixel-identical. **Live on build 14** (36°, at 76 % and 94 %): 0 opaque seam pixels, no checker strip (`shots/live3/cmp-r13-r14-line.png`, `cmp-r13-r14-crop1.png`). Known edge: while a view preview (`viewPreview`) is still loading, the preview canvas is hidden, so the gap shows checker over opaque pixels. Build 13 had the same behaviour.
- **Panel tab strip overflow**: Color, Swatches, Gradients and Patterns fill the 270 px dock, which pushed the Color group's ≡ menu and collapse chevron out of view. Tab labels now sit in a span that ellipsizes. Tabs have `min-width:0`, while the selected tab, the `.xd-editor-menu` wrapper and the collapse button are `flex:none` or don't shrink. The span exists because WebKit doesn't reliably ellipsize text directly inside a `<button>`.
- **Options bar scrollbar**: `.xd-photo-options` uses `overflow-x:auto`, and the global 8 px `::-webkit-scrollbar` added a row whenever the bar overflowed. That shifted the canvas and panels about 9 px. The scrollbar is now hidden, as `.xd-ps-taskbar-items` already does, and the bar still scrolls sideways.
- **Properties with a selection**: `transformBounds` comes from the engine's `transform_bounds`, which intersects the layer's content with the selection. A Single Row that misses every pixel gives `[0,0,0,0]`, so W/H/X/Y showed 0, and an X/Y edit would have moved the layer measured from 0. An empty frame now locks the Transform fields. Test in the layout suite's Properties case.
- **Observations, not changed**:
  - Window and Edit menus are taller than a 900 pt window minus the shell dock, so they scroll.
  - Right-click on a layer name selects its text.
  - The Properties transform fields stay in px when ruler units change (Task 28's open gap).
  - Tools without a hint (brush, pencil, eraser, Pattern Stamp) show the generic "Edits update every linked placement".
  - History snapshot thumbnails are placeholders (known gap).

## 2026-10-27 (cont.) — Claude / XDesign gap closure Phase 3, Task 29 detail

Branch: `validation/alpha-2026-09-14`. Uncommitted.

- **Engine API used** (`print_cmds.rs`): `print_pdf(&PrintPage{paper, image, rect, marks, description, label})` returns the PDF bytes. MediaBox is written `{pw:.2}`. `PrintImage{width, height, channels, data, icc}` takes 8-bit interleaved data with 1, 3 or 4 channels.
- **Host `pdf::photoshop_pdf`** (`xdesign_photo_pdf.rs`):
  - It clones the document into a temporary `Session`, so the user's history is never touched.
  - Modes other than RGB, Grayscale and CMYK run `image.mode.rgb` first.
  - RGB and Grayscale use `photocraft_compose::flatten(d).over_background([1,1,1])`.
  - CMYK runs `layer.flattenImage` and reads the single layer's surface, keeping the first `fmt.mode.color_channels()` of `fmt.channels()` per pixel. This drops alpha and spot channels.
  - Paper is `px × 72 / ppi`, with 72 ppi when the resolution is 0. Calling `print_pdf` directly skips `file.print`'s 36 pt minimum paper.
- **Host `xdesign_photo_export`**: `pdf` joins the extension list. The PDF branch adds the warning "Photoshop PDF keeps the flattened image; layers are not saved." when there is more than one layer. Both branches end in `photocraft_format::atomic_write`.
- **Artboards to PDF**: `file.export.artboardsToPdf {path, artboards?, quality}` is added to `command_supported`. It returns `{path, pages}`. The engine's `write_file` is already atomic, so the plan's temporary-file staging was dropped.
- **Frontend**:
  - `ImageExportDialog` takes `copy`. `COPY_FORMATS` puts PSD, then Photoshop PDF, then the Export As formats.
  - `exportOpen` is `"export" | "copy" | false`, and the dialog is keyed on it so switching modes resets the format.
  - `ArtboardsToPdfDialog` sends the selected artboard ids only when Export Selected Artboards is on.
- **Tests**: a Rust module test (RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab colour spaces, page size from ppi, a 1 px image at 0.24 pt), plus FileDialogs, ImageDialogs and fileMenu.studio cases.

Branch: `validation/alpha-2026-09-14`. Uncommitted.

- **Why host-side**: the pinned engine has no red-eye command. `xdesign_photo_red_eye.rs` handles `paint.redEye {x, y[, width, height], pupilSize, darken[, layer]}` before `engine.execute`.
- **Detection**:
  - A pixel is red when (r − max(g, b)) / r ≥ 0.35. Red pixels form 4-connected pupils, and specks under 4 px are ignored.
  - A click searches a square reaching an eighth of the shorter side (at least 16 px) and takes the nearest pupil.
- **Correction**:
  - The disc radius is 0.5–1.5 × the pupil's area radius, set by Pupil Size.
  - Inside the disc, reddish pixels blend toward (g + b) / 2, darkened by Darken Amount. The edge is anti-aliased and selection coverage is respected.
  - Only the corrected discs are rewritten.
- **History**: one journalled "Red Eye Tool" state. Finding nothing returns `{corrected:0}` with no step.
- **Limits**: RGB only. Boxes over 8 MP are refused.
- **Gesture**: a drag of 3 or more screen px on both axes is a box; anything smaller is a click.

## 2026-10-27 — Claude / XDesign gap closure Phase 2, Task 13 detail

Branch: `validation/alpha-2026-09-14`. Uncommitted.

Engine contracts (photocraft 47f9306, read-only: `crates/engine/src/warp_cmds.rs`, `crates/geom/src/warp.rs`):
- **Split, grid and remove commands are pure** when the warp is sent inline:
  - The commands are `edit.transform.splitWarpCrosswise|Vertically|Horizontally`, `edit.transform.removeWarpSplit` and `edit.transform.warpGrid`.
  - Params: `{rect, style, bend, hDistort, vDistort, vertical, mesh? (custom only), at|size}`.
  - Reply: `{warp:{style, bend, hDistort, vDistort, vertical, bounds, mesh:{us, vs, points}}}`. The document version doesn't change, so `runPhotoCommand` returns `reply.result`.
- **Split on a 1×1 custom mesh commits the thirds first.** A crosswise split at the centre gives a 4×4 mesh with knots 0, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 1. Presets are fitted as one patch first.
- **`removeWarpSplit`** removes the interior knot nearest `param_at(at)`, and picks u when du ≤ dv. The frontend therefore sends `at` halfway along the selected line's first patch, so a crossing line can't win.
- **`warpGrid` is square only** (`size` 1–64; it fits the current surface sampled at i/n).
- **BezierMesh**:
  - (3c+1)×(3r+1) control points, row-major.
  - `fit` uses `BERN_INV=[[1,0,0,0],[-5/6,3,-1.5,1/3],[1/3,-1.5,3,-5/6],[0,0,0,1]]`.
  - It is not reachable from the host.

Frontend (`src/apps/xdesign/photo/GeometryDialog.tsx`):
- `locateKnot`, `warpMeshPoint` (eval) and `fitWarpMesh` are exact TS ports of BezierMesh `locate`, `eval` and `fit`. `regridWarpMesh(mesh, cols, rows)` refits the current surface on even knots.
  - It exists because Photoshop's Custom Grid has separate columns and rows, but native `warpGrid` is square only.
  - Square sizes go to the engine. Non-square sizes refit locally: from the current custom mesh, or for a preset style from `warpGrid size 1` first.
- `warpGridId(mesh)` returns "1", "3", "4" or "5" only for even square meshes, otherwise "custom".
  - The select carries a hidden "custom" readout option, so choosing the "Custom" action option still fires when the readout is already Custom.
- `CustomGridSizeDialog` is portalled into `.xd-photo` as a sibling of the warp form, not inside it, because React synthetic submit and keydown events bubble through portals. It also calls stopPropagation on submit.
  - The `useDesignDialog` stack makes Escape close only the inner dialog.
- Handles ignore pointerdown while a split tool is armed, so a click on a handle still reaches the svg and splits there.
- `photo.css`:
  - `.xd-photo-warp-split`: transparent 9px stroke hit lines, accent when pressed or focused.
  - `.is-splitting`: crosshair cursor.
  - `.xd-photo-warp-split-tools`: the split button row.

Tests (`GeometryDialog.test.tsx`, "Photoshop warp split and grid options"):
- Refit preserves the surface.
- The grid options send the engine params, and Arc is regridded to custom.
- Custom Grid Size: clamp alert, local 4×2 refit, reopening shows 4/2, Escape closes only the inner dialog, 5×5 goes through the engine.
- Split arming, disarming and the handle click-through.
- Remove Warp Split's `at` for vertical and horizontal lines, including selection with Enter.

## 2026-10-25 — Claude / XDesign photo vs Photoshop 2026: missing editing features audit

Branch: `validation/alpha-2026-09-14`. Uncommitted. Full audit behind the summary in the matching PROGRESS.md entry; spot-checked against the engine and PhotoStudio before saving. Line numbers drift.

Legend: PRESENT = wording/context diff or exposed elsewhere. MISSING-UI = engine (photocraft rev 47f9306) has the command, XDesign has no UI. MISSING = needs engine work.
Sizes: S = UI-only/small, M = moderate, L = significant engine work.

KEY ARCHITECTURE FACT. The engine is the external `photocraft-engine` crate (rev 47f9306, checked out at
`~/.cargo/git/checkouts/photocraft-58992417ad0aec0a/47f9306/crates/engine/src`). It registers far more commands than XDesign wires up.
The host gate is `command_supported()` in `src-tauri/src/xdesign_photo.rs:684-762`: prefix allow-list (paint. select. layer. image. filter.
edit.transform. type. vector. path. channel. tools. shape. gradient. brush. color. pattern. layerComp. count. measurementLog. notes. style. tool.
cloneSource. slice. variables.) plus an explicit list of `edit.*` / `view.*` ids. NOT allowed today: every `file.*` (automate, scripts, export,
revert...), `edit.autoAlignLayers`, `edit.autoBlendLayers`, `edit.contentAwareFill`, `edit.defineBrushPreset`, `edit.defineCustomShape`,
`edit.findAndReplaceText`, `edit.checkSpelling`, `edit.toggleLastState`, `edit.purge.*`, `edit.keyboardShortcuts/menus/toolbar`.
So most "MISSING-UI (edit./file.)" items need a one-line allow-list change (S) plus the UI. Prefix-allowed families (layerComp., notes.,
count., measurementLog., slice., variables., cloneSource.) already pass the gate; they simply have zero frontend callers.
Menu spec is `PhotoStudio.tsx:~1060-1400 (line numbers drift; file is being edited)` (const `menus`); tool rail is `IMAGE_TOOL_GROUPS` in `src/apps/xdesign/editorTools.ts:12-34`;
panels are `ALL_PANELS` at `PhotoStudio.tsx:114-118`.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Tools (rail = editorTools.ts:12-34; 41 tools)

Photoshop tool -> status
- Move: PRESENT (rail). Artboard: MISSING-UI (engine `layer.new.artboard`, `layer.artboard.set`; Layer > New > Artboard... exists, PhotoStudio.tsx:1183) - no tool to draw/resize artboards. M

## 2026-09-16 — screenshot diagnosis: WebKit skipped the light glass block (whole-query fix superseded above)

User screenshot `NSIRD_screencaptureui_QMa6TU/Screenshot 2026-09-15 at 10.47.49 PM.png` showed fully opaque Glacier welcome card, menubar, dock and companion bubble despite prior alpha changes. Static HTTP inspection confirmed Vite was serving the updated 38% rules, but they were guarded by `@media not (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)`. MDN browser-compat-data marks that feature unsupported in Safari/WebKit; Media Queries 4 specifies unsupported-feature conditions evaluate to unknown, and condition-level negation leaves unknown. Thus that gate does not match on unsupported engines; the opaque baseline survives. Earlier CSS syntax/contrast checks did not catch this applicability bug.

Changed to whole-query negation `@media not all and (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)`, preserving supported `reduce` opt-out and the explicit app `.ot-reduce-glass` gate without requiring unsupported WebKit features. Also added missing `.ot-companion-bubble` to floating glass surfaces. Appearance now exposes an inline explanation and explicit **Enable glass** action when the saved Reduce transparency preference is on (light/Liquid themes); no silent setting reset, profile read or OS preference change. OS preference handling remains limited to engines that expose the media feature.

Checks: one clean tsc, CSS parsed (72 light rules / 91 settings rules), diff check, and a read of the live Vite stylesheet confirms the corrected gate/bubble selector are delivered. Added a regression assertion for query-level negation; **not executed**. No UI automation/native profile access/build/commit/release. Source/spec diagnosis is concrete; **the live native DOM's settings and post-fix visuals still need user verification**, not claimed measured.

Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/main/css/at-rules/media.json (`prefers-reduced-transparency`) · https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries-4/#evaluating · https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries-4/#mq-not .

## 2026-09-15 — Libraries.dev border integration: one material edge, stable renderer

Reproduced the user's dock screenshot with the real `Dock` and `metal-fx@2.0.10`. There was **no Beam instance**: our 2px base rim, 4px shader, brightness/saturation boost, vendor white inner rim/pseudo outline and native dock chrome formed multiple concentric borders. Compared the original Libraries.dev source at `422180dd7a5ac646c85deedc65500c4a74339127` (read-only clone under `/private/tmp/pi-github-repos/runtime-7egNy1/e08c332157be049d9fbd6358a8e7e600300bcd53c1985d33862e60db449cb6a2`) and the installed package/API.

The deeper resize/pause tests also exposed real failures, not just excessive styling: wrapper prop/resize handling can leave stale radii or erase paused canvases, its passive preset effect can freeze an older palette, and the renderer destructor's asynchronous `contextlost` callback targets the shared global singleton—an old context can mark a NEW renderer lost. ### 2026-06-24 (pt6) — XDesign: the final 3 (image-gen hardening · PPTX export · motion+video mode) — FEATURE-COMPLETE vs open-design
- **Shipped the last 3 gaps** (3 committed slices). Only multiplayer (not contested) + the live raster [P-AUTH] check now remain.
- **Image-gen hardening (P-AUTH risk reduction — can't live-test w/o a key):** `parse_openai_image` clearly explains a returned `data[0].url` (we request b64); `parse_imagen` accepts nested `image.imageBytes` / `inlineData.data` variants (+2 cargo). New `xdesign_save_bytes` Rust command (binary write to a chosen path) + ipc — used by PPTX + video export.
- **PPTX export (new dep `pptxgenjs@4.0.1`, approved):** `deckToPptx.ts` (+5 vitest) — `parseDeckSlides` regex-extracts title+bullets per `<section class=slide>` (`<li>` else `<p>` fallback; strips tags/entities), `isDeckHtml`, `deckColors` (brand bg/ink/accent via `seedFromDesignSystem`, bare RRGGBB). `deckToPptxBase64` lazy-imports pptxgenjs → native **editable** slides on a brand master (16:9, accent bar, title + bulleted body). `HtmlArtifactPreview` shows an **Export PPTX** button for decks.

The composer prompt was drafted by a background subagent (frontend-design lens).
- **v1 scope (deferred to later slices):** components/text-styles in the plan, multi-screen flows, real images (Adobe layer). v1 = one rich screen, color-variable design system, inline typography. **Caveat:** color variables aren't in the shape-history stack, so ⌘Z removes the shapes but leaves the (dedup-by-name) vars — harmless.
- **Smoke test (user, hot-reload):** XDesign → Claude rail → **✦ Generate** → type e.g. "a pricing page for a dev tool, dark & bold" → a full auto-layout design lands as editable frames; Variables panel shows the tokens; edit nodes; change the `brand` var to re-theme; ⌘Z removes the whole generation.

### 2026-06-14 — AAA Rebuild: Phase 3.4 layout systems → 🎉 3.4 COMPLETE (constraints · overrides · variants)
- **Pre-approved phase** (3.4 was inside the 2026-06-13 Phase-3 ranked plan). Built as 6 green TDD slices, each committed; all frontend → **hot-reloads, no `tauri dev` restart**. tsc / vitest / vite build gated on real exit codes every slice. **232 → 351 tests** (+119… actually +35 new xdesign tests on top of the 316 baseline).
- **Constraints** (`5793fc4` model+tests, `24ba600` wiring): new pure **`constraints.ts`** — `applyConstraints(child, oldFrame, newFrame)` solves H (left/right/left-right/center/scale) and V independently; `reflowConstraints` recursively replays descendant boxes from **drag-start snapshots** (never compounds) and **stops at auto-layout child frames** (their interior is `computeAutoLayout`'s job). Wired into `Canvas.tsx` resize: `onHandleMouseDown` snapshots `childStarts` for selected non-AL frames; the resize move-effect reflows them via `patchMany`. Inspector gets a **Constraints section** — Figma pin-box (clickable struts) + H/V dropdowns, both bound to `constraintH/V` so they can't drift; shown only when the parent is a non-AL frame. 20 constraints tests.
- **Non-lossy overrides** (`1148d22` model, `d9b0b45` wiring): `syncFromMain` no longer wipes local edits. Added `linkedNodeId` (the main-descendant id each clone mirrors — durable override key) + `overrides` (on the instance root) to ShapeBase. Pure **`overrides.ts`**: `findInstanceRoot`, `captureOverride` (allow-listed visual/text/size props diffed vs main → absolute, reset-to-main clears; x/y as **root-relative offsets**; never x/y on the root), `applyOverrides` (re-anchors position to the preserved root). `updateShape` captures; new pure **`recloneInstance`** re-clones + re-applies (main wins for untouched props, override wins where edited). New `resetInstanceOverrides` action + Inspector **"Reset overrides"** (reachable from any node in the instance). 14 overrides + 4 instanceSync tests (edit-survives-sync, main-wins-on-non-overridden, position re-anchor, map persistence).
- **Variants** (`8bee045` model, `c444209` swap+UI): `isVariantSet` (container frame) / `variantProps` (member main) / `variantSelection` (instance) on ShapeBase. Pure **`variants.ts`**: `variantProperties` (derive prop→values), `resolveVariant` (exact → nearest → first), `defaultSelection`. **`setVariantSelection`** re-points the instance to the resolved member + re-clones (position + override map preserved; `recloneInstance` strips the member's `variantProps`/`isVariantSet` off the root and keeps `variantSelection`). `createInstance` of a member seeds the root's selection. New `toggleVariantSet` + `setVariantProps`. Inspector: **Variant-set toggle** on frames, a `Name=value` **props editor** on member mains, a **per-property dropdown** on an instance in a set (swaps via the root). 9 variants + 5 store-level swap tests.
- **Known v1 limits** (noted in tracker): override capture fires on `updateShape` only — **canvas drag / `patchMany` don't record overrides**; overrides **don't carry across a variant swap** (keyed by member node ids). Both are reasonable follow-ups.

Magenta anchor squares + handle lines/dots render in screen space (`PathEditOverlay`, a sibling of `ResizeHandles`); resize/rotation handles are suppressed while editing to avoid conflict.
- **New `DragOp` variant `anchor`** (pathId/index/part); mousemove maps the cursor → unit space via the new **`worldToUnit`** inverse of `localToWorld` (both now exported from `booleanOps.ts`), **correct under rotation + flip** — round-trip unit-tested, and the flip math provably matches the render's world-space center-mirror (`x+(1-u)*w`). One undo step per drag (pushHistory at start, per-move via existing `updateShape`, no history spam).
- **Known v1 limits**: editing operates on the **primary contour** (boolean-result holes/subpaths aren't draggable yet); the bbox doesn't reflow during edit (points may drift outside 0..1 — renders fine, but the cyan selection box won't re-hug until a resize). Both noted for a later slice.

### 2026-06-13 — AAA Rebuild: Phase 3.3a — vector booleans (union/subtract/intersect/exclude)
- **Session recovery first**: prior session (`cec3ed1e`) was lost to a Cursor restart+update. Transcripts intact on disk; nothing lost — it had shipped 3.2 (committed) and only got as far as `npm install polygon-clipping` before a rate-limit + the restart. Resumed execution from there.

- **`booleanOps.ts`** (pure, 11 tests): `shapeToRing` flattens any shape to an absolute-space polygon — rect corners, 64-sample ellipse, bezier-flattened path (16/seg), bbox fallback for frame/text/image — honoring **rotation + flip**. `booleanShapes(op, shapes)` runs the op (subtract = bottom-most minus the union above it, so operands must be z-ordered bottom-first), then normalizes the `MultiPolygon` result back into ONE `PathShape` in unit space; holes / disjoint regions become extra rings.
- **PathShape gains additive `subpaths?: PathPoint[][]` + `fillRule?`** (even-odd so holes punch through) — backward-compatible, old paths hydrate unchanged. `pathToSvgD` appends each subpath as its own `M…Z`; the `<path>` sets `fill-rule`. (Boolean results are flattened polylines — no beziers — which is standard.)
- **`store.booleanOp(op, ids)`**: pushHistory → builds the result path inheriting the **bottom-most** shape's style (fill/stroke/gradient/opacity) + z-position + parent, removes operands **and their descendants** (no orphaned `parentId`), selects the result. One undo step.
- **UI**: Inspector multi-select block gains a **Boolean row** (Union/Subtract/Intersect/Exclude, `.xd-bool-row`); empty results (e.g. intersect of disjoint shapes) **toast** instead of failing silently.

### 2026-06-09 — Fix garbled Claude Code terminal + WebGL crisp rendering
- **Symptom:** the embedded Claude Code tab (and shell terminal) rendered the TUI distorted — stacked duplicate "Welcome back" banners + `�`-garbled glyphs (screenshot). Three root causes, all fixed:
  1. **UTF-8 chunk-boundary corruption (`terminal.rs`):** the pty reader did `String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..n])` per 8 KB read. Claude's Ink TUI is full of box-drawing/emoji multi-byte chars; any that straddled the read boundary got mangled into U+FFFD permanently. Fix: a **carry buffer** + new pure `incomplete_tail_len()` holds back an incomplete trailing UTF-8 sequence (≤3 bytes) until the next read. 4 unit tests incl. a round-trip that splits a box-drawing+emoji string at every byte offset and asserts no replacement chars.
  2. **Resize storm + bad initial size → stacked banners:** `fit.fit()` ran immediately on open (before layout/font settled), spawned `claude` at wrong cols/rows, then an undebounced `ResizeObserver` spammed pty resizes — each made Ink repaint mid-layout, landing frames below the last instead of overwriting. Fix: **debounced** fit (80ms), **change-guarded** pty resize (skip identical cols/rows), `await document.fonts.ready` before the first fit, and a **zero-size guard** (`waitForSize`) so we never fit a 0×0 container.
  3. **WebGL renderer** (user-requested, only new feature): added `@xterm/addon-webgl@^0.19.0` for crisp GPU text, with `onContextLoss`→dispose graceful fallback to the DOM renderer.
- **Refactor:** the two near-identical 180-line terminal components (`Terminal.tsx`, `ClaudeCodePanel.tsx`) now share **`src/apps/orion/ptyTerminal.ts`** (`attachPtyTerminal`) — all rendering/resize logic lives in one place. Components are ~40 lines each; `Terminal.tsx` keeps its `setPtyId` store wiring via `onOpened`/`onClosed`.
- ⚠️ Needs a **`tauri dev` restart** (Rust reader-thread change in `terminal.rs`). Frontend hot-reloads. tsc / cargo check / cargo terminal tests (4) / **99 frontend tests** / vite build all green. Runtime/UI human-unverified (agent can't run Tauri).

### 2026-06-05 — Hermes: surface the REAL agent error + usage diagnosis
- **Bug:** every swarm agent showed "agent exited with an error". Root cause: `run_agent` only reported **stderr**, but the CLI delivers run-level failures (usage/rate limits, API errors, max-turns) in the stream-json **`result` event** (with `is_error`/`subtype`/`api_error_status`), not stderr — which is empty, so we always fell back to the generic string. Fixed: capture the result-event error (`result_error`) and treat `is_error || subtype != "success"` as failure regardless of exit code; the UI now shows the actual reason. cargo green.
- **Usage diagnosis (why a swarm devastates the quota, even on Sonnet/Max-5x):** each agent is a full Claude Code subprocess that auto-loads the project context. Measured: a trivial **"ok"** call with the engine's exact flags cost **$0.23** and **~78k tokens** (60,892 cache-creation + 16,836 read) — because cwd=the repo pulls in **CLAUDE.md (~45k tokens / 940 lines)** + the user memory dir (~5k) + skills + MCP schemas, re-read every turn, ×N agents in parallel. Agents also inherit claude-code's full toolset incl. **Workflow/Task/`deep-research`**, so one agent can self-spawn a whole fan-out (the earlier "deep-research workflow running…" was exactly that). Model choice is minor next to this.
- **Mitigations (offered, not yet applied — tradeoffs):** run swarm agents in a clean cwd (drops CLAUDE.md/memory — biggest win, loses project context); `--strict-mcp-config` (drop global MCP servers); `--max-turns N` (bound runaway); restrict tools (`--disallowed-tools Workflow,Task…` so agents can't recursively fan out); smaller swarms / Haiku workers; and trim CLAUDE.md's old log (cuts ~45k tokens from every agent AND every Claude Code session).

### 2026-06-04 — Hermes: 4th app — a multi-agent orchestration Kanban (ROSIE orchestrates above it)
- **What it is:** a new in-canvas app `hermes` (amber accent, `Workflow` icon) — a Kanban where each task can fan out to a **parallel swarm** of headless `claude` agents. ROSIE is the meta-orchestrator above it: she plans/creates/arranges cards via MCP tools but **never dispatches** (approval gate — the user clicks Dispatch). NOTE: this is its own project, unrelated to the Nous Research "Hermes" gateway / Animus mac-mini work; the name collision is coincidental. A "Hermes agent" = a `claude --print --output-format stream-json` subprocess (reuses `claude_cli` plumbing: augmented PATH, Opus, Orion MCP config attached so swarm agents get Orion-aware tools). No external dependency, no HTTP endpoint, no mock — real agents on the subscription CLI.
- **Data (migration 0015):** `hermes_tasks` (cards: column backlog|ready|running|review|done|blocked, status, parent_id for sub-tasks, created_by user|rosie) + `hermes_agents` (swarm members: prompt, status, output, session_id, position). db.ts helpers + `useHermes` store (Map-based, like notesStore). Board state lives in orion.db (decision: local SQLite, not a shared backend).
- **Engine (`src-tauri/src/hermes.rs`):** `hermes_dispatch_task` reads dispatchable agents (status idle/failed/cancelled), spawns one subprocess per agent IN PARALLEL, streams each agent's assistant text via `hermes:agent` events + status via `hermes:agentStatus`, and rolls the task up (`maybe_finalize_task`: all completed→review, any failed→blocked, any cancelled→ready) via `hermes:task`. Engine is the sole DB writer during a run (frontend mirrors events; persists results so they survive relaunch). `hermes_stop_agent`/`hermes_stop_task` cancel via a Notify map. Boot `load()` reconciles agents/tasks left 'running' by a previous quit back to re-dispatchable. cache-invalidation uses `refresh()` (not `load()`) so ROSIE's MCP writes don't clobber a live swarm.
- **ROSIE tools (mcp_server.rs):** `orion_hermes_list_tasks` / `get_task` (gather results) / `create_task` / `add_agent` / `update_task` / `move_task` / `decompose` — all DB-only; `move_task`/`create_task` REJECT column='running' (dispatch is user-only). `orion_open_app` now accepts 'hermes'. EventBridge invalidation keyed on `isOrionHermesWriteTool`.
- **UI:** `src/apps/hermes/HermesApp.tsx` (6-column board, drag between columns except running, per-card dispatch/stop + agent pips + ROSIE badge) + `HermesTaskDetail.tsx` (drawer: editable title/prompt, swarm list with per-agent live streaming output + stop, add agent, dispatch all). `.hm-*` CSS in tokens.css, `--neon-amber`/`--hermes-accent` tokens.
- ⚠️ Needs a full **`tauri dev` restart** (new migration 0015 + new Rust module/commands — Rust rebuild, not just frontend hot-reload). All green: cargo check / tsc / **99 tests** (added matcher + store-reducer tests) / vite build. HermesApp is its own 8.3KB lazy chunk. Runtime/UI human-unverified (agent can't run Tauri). Approval-gate is enforced both in the UI (only user Dispatch calls the engine) and in ROSIE's tools (can't set 'running').

(3) phone sets `isIdleTimerDisabled` while a turn runs (screen won't auto-lock → app won't suspend → link won't drop mid-wait) + a 90s timeout that fails the pending bubble; a bad/expired session id is cleared on error so it can't poison future turns.

### 2026-06-02 — Archives companion: fix R.O.S.I.E "stuck on thinking" (helper claude stdin hang)
- Symptom: phone connected, asked R.O.S.I.E, stuck on "thinking…" forever (no reply, no error). Bisected on the Mac: `claude --print "…"` hangs when its stdin never reaches EOF, but returns in ~2.5s with `< /dev/null`. The helper's `Process` inherited the GUI app's (never-closing) stdin, so `claude --print` blocked indefinitely → no `chatReply`/`chatError` ever sent.
- Fix: `proc.standardInput = FileHandle.nullDevice` (immediate EOF) + `proc.currentDirectoryURL = home` in the helper's `runClaude`. `claude` is at `~/.local/bin/claude` (already covered by the augmented PATH). Helper rebuilds; re-run it (frontend unchanged). Lesson for any future CLI spawn from a GUI/agent process: always set stdin to nullDevice unless you're feeding it.

### 2026-06-02 — Archives companion: first on-device test + helper advertising fix
- User ran `ArchivesiOS` on a real iPhone — Phase 0 screen correct (advertising + "Searching for your Mac…") but no connection. Ran a 16-agent adversarial audit workflow (5 dimensions, each finding verified by a skeptic): 6 confirmed, all one root cause + its fallout.
- **Root cause:** the macOS helper's `sync.start()` sat in a `.task` on the `MenuBarExtra` content, which SwiftUI realizes only when the status item is first CLICKED → the Mac never advertised at launch (phone searches forever). iOS works because `RootView` starts in `.onAppear`. Rebuilds clean (`xcodebuild`, Swift 6, no concurrency warnings). Remaining user prereqs: grant macOS **Local Network** privacy to the helper (run the built `.app` from Finder if the prompt won't surface under Xcode for an LSUIElement agent), set `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` for a stable code identity so the grant sticks.

### 2026-05-31 — Companion: drag ragdoll (procedural limp & sway)
- Dragging her now makes her ragdoll (user picked the no-dep procedural route over a physics engine). New `dragState.ts` — a plain mutable singleton (NOT a store; drag is ~60Hz, no React renders) holding `{dragging, vx, vy}`. `CompanionAvatar` drag handlers write it (onStart/onDrag set dragging+velocity, onEnd clears dragging).
- `RosieModel` reads it each frame and drives a **damped-spring pendulum swing** of the whole body toward the drag motion: target tilt ∝ drag velocity (clamped ±0.7/±0.5 rad), semi-implicit Euler spring (K=95, C=11 → underdamped so she overshoots/flops), velocity decays when held still so she settles upright; release → spring keeps momentum and flops back to 0. Applied as a parent `swingRef` group rotation (rig-axis-independent → no T-pose risk). Secondary floppiness: Spine/Head get extra lag (∝ swingZ) + a forward slump while actually held, layered after the mixer so she reads limp, not rigid. Idle keeps playing underneath (full weight) to avoid the bind-pose bleed.
- tsc / build / 91 tests green. ⚠️ Visual/tuning unverified (agent can't run Tauri). Tunable knobs: swing gain 0.22, clamps, K/C, secondary magnitudes, and the pivot (currently her mid-body — could raise toward the head for more of a "dangling" feel). Skipped a review workflow — logic (spring stability, signal flow) verified analytically; the rest is look-and-feel for the user to tune. **Next:** proactive "asks a question" gesture.
- **T-pose bug fixed (root cause confirmed in three.js source).** When a fidget ended, the idle was revived with a bare `r.idle.fadeIn(0.4)`. But `AnimationAction._updateWeight` sets `enabled=false` once an action fades to weight 0, after which `_update` early-returns and `fadeIn`/`_scheduleFading` never re-enable it → idle never came back → bones fell to bind pose (T-pose), which also made the randoms appear to stop. Fix: set `r.idle.enabled = true` **before** `fadeIn`. (Idle time is frozen while disabled, so it resumes seamlessly.)
- **User clip→event mapping wired** (`RosieModel`): idle = **Idle_15** loop (unchanged) + random fidgets keep firing; **spawn-in = Fall4** one-shot when she appears (`companionVisible` false→true incl. first mount; note: if Fall4 ends prone we can chain `Arise`); **error/frustrated = Angry_To_Tantrum_Sit** one-shot on a failed turn (`rosie.error` onset); **thinking/working/listening = procedural look-around** (organic head/neck yaw+pitch layered on Idle_15 via post-multiply, eased by mode). New rig fields: `queue` (priority one-shots, play in any mode, via `startClipOnce`), `head`/`neck` bones, `lookW`, `lastVisible`/`lastErr` transition trackers.
- **Proactive "asks a question" = a gesture** — still TODO (needs the proactive trigger system; next). Look-around axis (assumed local Y=yaw / X=pitch) is human-unverified — may need axis tweak. tsc / build / 91 tests green. (Skipped a 5th review workflow — verified the one correctness-critical fix directly at the three.js source level; the rest is visual/tunable.)

### 2026-05-30 — Media viewer in Orion (images/video/audio render instead of the UTF-8 error)
- **Clicking an image in the file tree opened it in Monaco** → `read_file`'s `read_to_string` failed with "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" (a blank pane with an error string). Now media files render in a proper viewer.
- **New Rust `read_file_base64(path)`** (`fs_ops.rs`): validates exists/not-dir, caps at 20MB (`TOO_LARGE:<bytes>` sentinel past it), returns base64 (reuses `claude_cli::base64_encode`, made `pub(crate)`). Registered in `lib.rs`; `ipc.readFileBase64`. Frontend builds a `data:<mime>;base64,…` URL — works for ANY project path without widening the `asset://` scope (the scope is `$APPDATA/assets/**`).
- **`lib/mediaTypes.ts`** (pure, 9 tests): `extensionOf` (basename + `lastIndexOf('.')>0` so dotfiles → "") + `mediaTypeForPath` → `{kind,mime}|null` over an extension map (png/jpg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/avif/apng, mp4/m4v/webm/mov/ogv, mp3/wav/ogg/oga/opus/m4a/aac/flac, pdf). **`OrionMediaViewer`**: checkerboard backdrop, Fit/1:1 toggle, name·kind·dims·size toolbar, media-aware tab icons. `OrionApp` registry routes `case "file"` to the viewer when `mediaTypeForPath` is non-null, else `OrionEditor`. Editor's UTF-8 error path now shows a friendly "Can't show this as text — binary file" for non-media binaries.
- **Ran a 4-dimension adversarial review** (16 agents). 12 raised → 3 confirmed, all fixed:
  1. **SVG regression** — SVG was routed to the read-only image viewer, but it's valid UTF-8 and routinely hand-edited. Dropped `svg` from the media map → stays editable XML in Monaco (`lang.ts` maps it to xml). It never hit the UTF-8 error, so it was a pure loss of capability.
  2. **PDF blanked silently** — `data:` PDFs in an `<iframe>` render as an empty white pane on macOS WKWebView (the exact silent-white-pane class the WebPreview tab fixed earlier). PDFs now render an **"Open externally" card** (via `openPath`, no iframe, no byte read) — reliable. Added `opener:allow-open-path` to capabilities.
  3. **Silent media-load failures** — corrupt/unsupported-codec files (HEVC `.mov`, truncated png) left a blank stage forever. Added `onError` to img/video/audio → friendly message + an "Open externally" button.
- **Deferred:** inline PDF rendering (would need pdf.js or a verified path); large media rides a 20MB data-URL cap (a streamed custom protocol is the upgrade if big video matters). tsc / cargo / build / 91 tests green. ⚠️ capabilities + Rust changed → needs a full `tauri dev` restart to exercise.

### 2026-05-30 — Preview tab: surface unreachable URLs + fix the silent-no-op reload button
- **Web preview was leaving a white pane** when the dev server wasn't reachable — no error, no signal. Now `WebPreview` tracks an `onLoad` event (which fires for any HTTP response, including 4xx/5xx); if 5s pass with no load, it surfaces a clear "Couldn't reach <url> — is your dev server running on this port?" overlay with a Retry button. (Tauri CSP is `null`, so CSP isn't the blocker; the silent failure mode was just bad UX for the common case of "I haven't started npm run dev yet" or "wrong port".)
- **Reload button did nothing**: it called `setUrl(url)` with the unchanged value → Zustand value-equality short-circuited → no re-render → iframe key (memoized on `[url]` with `Date.now()` at first render) never recomputed → no remount. Fix: added `reloadNonce` + a `reload()` action to the preview store; iframe key derives from `[url, reloadNonce]`. Toolbar reload button + retry-overlay button both call it. The unreachable timeout also resets on `reloadNonce` change so retry actually re-arms the 5s window.

### 2026-05-30 — Two real bugs hit while dogfooding: Claude Code session loss on tab switch + missing file-tree auto-refresh
- **Claude Code tab kept dying on every tab switch** despite the `persistent` opt-in. Root cause was structural: the workspace renderer put the active tab in a *different* DOM parent (`.ot-panel-tab-slot.active`) than the persistent-inactive ones (`.ot-panel-tab-slot`). When the user switched away, React couldn't reconcile the Claude Code component across that parent boundary — it **unmounted** the outgoing instance (cleanup → `terminalKill` → pty dies, fresh `ulid` ptyId on next mount) before remounting it as a hidden sibling. Fix: render every mounted tab (active + other persistent) as **siblings in one keyed list** in `.ot-panel-tabs-layer`; `.active` becomes a pure CSS toggle. Pty stays alive across switches now.
- **File tree never reflected Claude Code's edits** (user had to relaunch the app to see them). The existing `useFileTreeRefresh` bump only fires on `claude:event` tool_results — fine for the chat rails, useless for the Claude Code tab since its tool calls happen *inside* the interactive pty (no stream-json hits the frontend). Fix: throttled global listener on `terminal:data` → leading-edge `useFileTreeRefresh.bump()` every 750ms during continuous output, with a final bump 750ms after output settles. No new deps. Bonus: also catches raw shell commands (`npm i`, `mv`, etc.) that touch project files.
- **Still missing** (deliberate): external-editor changes don't refresh the tree (would need a real `notify`-based file watcher; new Rust dep — flagged for if/when you want it).

### 2026-05-28 — Fix: moving a frame orphaned its children (frames now carry contents)
- **Bug surfaced testing Phase 3 components:** after `createInstance`, repositioning a frame via `update {x}` (or the inspector) left its accent/title behind — agent saw "children that didn't move with their instance" / strays at x=414. Root cause: positions are absolute and `updateShape` was a flat single-shape patch — only the canvas DRAG path moved descendants (via `patchMany` + `collectDescendantIds`).
- **Fix:** `updateShape` now, when x and/or y change, translates the shape's descendants by the same delta (frames carry their contents). Matches the drag path; fixes BOTH the inspector and agent `update`. Non-position patches don't cascade. Drag is unaffected (it uses `patchMany` directly, not `updateShape`).
- `createInstance` gained an optional `at:{x,y}` (op: `createInstance {mainId, x?, y?}`) so the agent can place instances directly instead of all stacking at `main.x + w + 40` (the cause of the "rogue duplicate frames at 390,200" pileup). Also removed the no-op `s.id===mainId ? s.x+dx : s.x+dx` ternary (always shifted whole subtree anyway — clone was fine; the stray children came from the later `update`, not the clone).
- Tests 70→72: move-frame-carries-child (child x 20→320 with a +300 frame move); createInstance-at places the whole subtree (child at 510, not left behind). tsc / cargo / build green.
